audio.strategy: One AudioContext (src/audio/audioEngine.ts). Two Piano layers (A, B) each own their voices and route only to their own layer bus. Each layer bus passes through an ordered effect chain — Mod 1 -> Mod 2 -> Delay -> Amp Sim/EQ (or Filter) -> Compressor -> Reverb — then a per-layer level gain into the master gain -> DynamicsCompressor limiter -> the single AudioContext.destination. A single shared Rotary sits AFTER reverb (reverb always precedes rotary); a layer whose Amp Sim/EQ model is 'To Rotary' has its post-reverb signal rerouted into the shared rotary and out of the normal master path. Grand/Upright/Electric play RECORDED multi-sampled buffers (nearest recorded root, playback-rate pitch, <=1 semitone shift); Clav/Digital/Misc play HONEST SYNTHESIS. KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Timbre, Unison, and Soft Release shape each voice; sustain (UI/keyboard/MIDI CC64) holds released notes per layer only when that layer's SUSTPED is on. Every functional Piano, Layer-Effects, and Master control maps to real audio via src/audio/controlBindings.ts; Organ, Synth, and Program controls are not bound and stay decorative. Parameter changes use short ~20ms ramps to avoid clicks; voices, effect units, and the AudioContext are all cleaned up on release/teardown.

notes: The recorded sample sets are bundled under public/samples/ and load offline (no network at runtime). scripts/fetch-samples.mjs reproducibly re-downloads them; provenance is echoed in each set's manifest.json and public/samples/LICENSE.txt.

Each recorded set uses 30 root notes spaced a minor third apart, so playback pitch-shifts a note by at most ~1 semitone (no obvious stretching). Only a single recorded velocity layer per root note is bundled; velocity/KB-Touch/Dyn-Comp shaping at play time is declared honestly and is NOT presented as multiple recorded velocity layers.
If a sample set fails to load, the engine reports a labeled playable fallback (StatusBar) and plays the synthesized 'digital' recipe instead of pretending recordings exist.

Master Level, all functional Piano controls, and all Layer-Effects controls change rendered audio and agree with their panel feedback (tests: tests/instruments.test.ts, tests/pianoControls.test.ts, tests/effects.test.ts, tests/controlBindings.test.ts).

The audio boundary is exercised in tests with node-web-audio-api's OfflineAudioContext (real rendered signals), not mocks. The Phase-1 fake backend (src/audio/fakeBackend.ts) still backs the preserved Phase-1 tests.

Organ, Synth, and Program controls remain honestly decorative in Phase 2: they move/press and store presentation-only state (src/state/controlStore.ts) and are not bound in src/audio/controlBindings.ts.

decorativeControls.summary: Organ, Synth, and Program controls stay decorative in Phase 2 (they have stable IDs, accessible names/roles/values, respond to pointer and keyboard, and show state, but change no audio or system state). The Piano section, the Layer Effects section, and the Master Level knob are now functional.
decorativeControls.inventory: src/model/controls.ts (CONTROLS); presentation state in src/state/controlStore.ts; functional bindings in src/audio/controlBindings.ts.

functional.keybed: 73 keys (E1..E7), pointer + independent multi-touch + accessible computer keyboard + Web MIDI note/velocity + CC64 sustain, through one shared note lifecycle (src/input/noteRouter.ts) into the single-context AudioEngine.
functional.piano: Six selectable types (Grand/Upright/Electric recorded; Clav/Digital/Misc synth), two layers (enable/focus/level/octave/SUSTPED/PSTICK with per-layer voice ownership), KB Touch (3 curves), Dyn Comp (Off/1/2/3), Timbre (per family), Unison (Off/1/2/3), Soft Release, String Res, and a labeled playable fallback.
functional.layerEffects: Per-layer chains for Piano A and B (Mod 1, Mod 2, Delay, Amp Sim/EQ, Compressor, Reverb) plus a shared Rotary via To Rotary; FX focus follows/overrides layer focus, Piano group mode, Delay/Compressor/Reverb global mode, per-unit bypass, all-effects bypass, and the documented signal order.
functional.master: Master Level knob drives the single master gain feeding the limiter and the one destination.
